judgment.rationale: Both indicators sit under Content Standard B4.1.1.1 (quantities and place value for multi-digit whole numerals up to 100,000) in BASIC 4 (same rank 0), so direction rests on statement content, not code or rank order. B4.1.1.1.1 and its LCs cover concrete/representational modelling of number quantities and place value with graph sheets or multi-base materials up to 100,000; B4.1.1.1.2 and its LCs cover reading and writing those numbers in figures and in words up to 100,000. Understanding of place-value structure built through modelling substantively supports success in the symbolic/verbal naming and recording of the same number range, a move from concrete representation to standard numeral and word notation. Same-rank direction is therefore justified by this concrete-to-symbolic content shift rather than by shared parentage; both endpoints' source evidence is truncated, which limits exemplar detail but does not conflict with the statement text.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 5 Indicators (same Grade rank 1) in Strand 1 Number, but in different Sub-Strands: B5.1.3.1.1 'Determine equivalent fractions of given fractions' (Sub-Strand 3: Number: Fractions, under the Content Standard on comparing/adding/subtracting/multiplying fractions) and B5.1.1.3.1 'Identify the factors of whole numbers 1 - 100' (Sub-strand 1: Counting, Representation & Cardinality, under the Content Standard on factors, multiples, composite/even/odd/prime numbers). Their LCs share only the generic tag 'number' (jaccard 0.17) and the token 'of', so lexical/code-prefix and shared-ancestor signals alone carry no semantic weight. There is genuine conceptual coherence: multiplicative structure and common-factor reasoning underpins generating and reducing equivalent fractions, so the two skills reinforce one another within Number. However, the bounded indicator texts do not state that equivalent-fraction work is expressed through factors or simplest form, and both statements sit at the same grade rank, so the evidence does not substantiate a directional dependency in either orientation; symmetric relatesTo is the supported judgment. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each), so a stronger developmental link could exist in unseen exemplars.
